name: Micro-USB (Micro-B)
description: The 5-pin Micro-B connector on countless older phones, dev boards, and battery packs. Same USB 2.0 signals as USB-A (VBUS, D-, D+, GND) plus a 5th 'ID' pin that selects USB On-The-Go host vs device role. Being superseded by USB-C, but still everywhere on hobby hardware.

contacts.name: ID
contacts.description: OTG role select: floating = device (default), shorted to GND (pin 5) = host

variants: Micro-A (host) and Micro-B (device) share this pinout; the difference is the shell shape and the ID pin state. Most cables/devices are Micro-B.
USB 3.0 Micro-B (on old USB3 hard drives) is this connector plus a second bank of 5 SuperSpeed pins alongside -- a wider, two-part shell.
gotchas: The ID pin (4) is what makes OTG work: a special OTG cable ties ID to GND so the device becomes a USB host and can drive a keyboard/flash drive. A normal charge/sync cable leaves ID floating.

Data-only vs charge-only cables: cheap 'charging' micro-USB cables often omit D+/D- entirely, so a device that needs USB data enumeration just charges and never connects. Meter the cable if a board won't be seen.
The connector is fragile -- the tiny solder tabs lift off dev boards with repeated plugging; strain-relieve it.
notes: USB 2.0 Micro-B 5-pin (VBUS/D-/D+/ID/GND) per the USB spec. ID pin OTG behaviour noted.
